title: AI/NLP Engine to Detect Serious Injury & Fatality (SIF) Precursors in OIL's Unsafe-Act/Unsafe-Condition and Near-Miss Reports
description:
• Background OIL collects large volumes of UA/UC observations, near-miss and incident reports through its HSSE platform but these are triaged manually after certain time intervals such as monthly, quarterly etc.However, Global best practice (DEKRA Martin & Black 2015; EEI SIF Precursor model; VelocityEHS 2024 PSIF classifier) has established that low-severity incidents do not share the same causes as fatalities - non-fatal US accidents fell 51% over 15 years while fatalities fell only 25.5%.Leading operators therefore separately flag the ~20–25% of reports carrying genuine fatal potential.
Problem Description Build a prototype that ingests OIL's free-text safety reports and automatically a) Classifies each as SIF-potential vs non-SIF-potential b) Tags it to the relevant IOGP Life-Saving Rule (e.g., Energy Isolation, Hot Work,Confined Space, Line of Fire)
c) Surfaces recurring precursor patterns (activity, location, barrier failure) via a dashboard.
Expected Outcome/Solution A working AI/NLP with an interactive dashboard that ranks sites/activities by SIF-precursor density and auto-maps to Life-Saving Rules, enabling HSE to focus interventions where fatal potential is highest.
Relevant Data Availability (if any)
OIL's UA/UC observations, near-miss and incident reports.
summary: Innovation (4/5): draws on ai, nlp applied to a miscellaneous problem, placing it in the breakthrough band. Feasibility (4/5): as a software build with moderate integration complexity, a working prototype is realistic in a 36-hour window. Impact (3/5): addresses a more targeted user group within Miscellaneous. Tech Depth (3/5): centers on model. Sustainability (4/5): has a clear long-term maintenance path. Scalability (2/5): currently scoped narrowly and would need rework to scale. Total 20/30 -> Yellow verdict.

detail.title: AI/NLP Engine to Detect Serious Injury & Fatality (SIF) Precursors in OIL's Unsafe-Act/Unsafe-Condition and Near-Miss Reports

overview.in_plain_terms: Build an NLP tool that reads Oil India's free-text safety reports and automatically flags the roughly 20-25% that carry genuine fatal potential, tagging each to the relevant safety rule and surfacing recurring patterns, so safety teams can focus intervention where it actually matters most.
overview.why_it_matters: Research shows low-severity incidents and fatalities don't share the same root causes, non-fatal accidents have fallen much faster than fatalities industry-wide. Separately flagging genuine fatal-potential reports lets safety teams focus where intervention actually saves lives.
pain_points: Large volumes of unsafe-act/unsafe-condition and near-miss reports are currently triaged manually at slow intervals (monthly, quarterly).
Low-severity incidents and fatalities have genuinely different root causes, but current triage doesn't separate them.
Recurring precursor patterns (activity, location, barrier failure) aren't systematically surfaced for targeted intervention.
overview.background: Global safety research (DEKRA, EEI SIF model, VelocityEHS) shows fatal-potential incidents have distinct causal patterns from low-severity ones, but OIL's current manual, periodic triage doesn't separate them, missing an opportunity for targeted, life-saving intervention.
overview.whats_being_asked: An AI/NLP prototype classifying free-text safety reports as SIF-potential versus non-SIF-potential, tagging them to IOGP Life-Saving Rules, and surfacing recurring precursor patterns via a dashboard.
expected_solution: SIF-potential vs. non-SIF-potential classification from free-text reports.
Automatic tagging to relevant IOGP Life-Saving Rules.
Recurring precursor pattern surfacing (activity, location, barrier failure).
Interactive dashboard ranking sites/activities by SIF-precursor density.

analysis.innovation_scope_note: Moderate-High. Applying the SIF-precursor distinction (grounded in real, cited industry research) via NLP classification is a genuine, well-motivated, technically sound application.
analysis.invention_effort_note: Moderate. Achievable using established text-classification NLP techniques; real effort in correctly grounding classification criteria in the cited SIF-precursor research frameworks.

competitive_landscape.note: Very specific industrial-safety NLP application, narrow field appropriate for a team willing to research the cited safety science.

innovation.note: Genuine application of a research-grounded distinction (SIF-potential vs. general severity) via NLP is real, well-motivated technical work.

invention.note: Achievable using established text-classification techniques, real effort in accurate SIF-precursor criteria grounding.

technical_feasibility.note: No hard external data dependency beyond constructing realistic sample safety reports; established NLP techniques are well-supported.

impact_and_benefits.note: Directly supports focusing safety intervention where fatal potential is genuinely highest, a real, life-relevant impact case.

architecture.note: Text classification plus tagging plus dashboard visualization, well-understood pattern applied to a well-grounded problem.

overall_verdict.reasoning: Strong pick, genuinely well-motivated with real cited research grounding. Research the actual IOGP Life-Saving Rules and SIF-precursor criteria (referenced sources: DEKRA Martin & Black, EEI SIF model) to ground your classification logic accurately, not an invented severity heuristic.

evaluator_lens.biggest_strength: Very well-grounded in cited, real industry safety research (DEKRA, EEI SIF model, VelocityEHS), giving a credible, research-based foundation rather than an arbitrary classification scheme.
evaluator_lens.biggest_risk: Building a generic severity classifier without genuine grounding in the specific SIF-precursor research criteria named would miss the actual point, distinguishing fatal-potential causes from general severity, not just flagging 'bad' reports.
evaluator_lens.validate_before_commit: Research the actual IOGP Life-Saving Rules and the cited SIF-precursor frameworks (the referenced research explicitly named in the PS) to ground your classification criteria accurately, rather than building a generic text-severity classifier.

Construct realistic sample safety reports (free-text) spanning both genuine SIF-potential and non-SIF-potential scenarios.

prototype_4_22: Build your SIF-potential classification model grounded in real research criteria.
Build IOGP Life-Saving Rule tagging logic.
Start precursor pattern extraction (activity, location, barrier failure) from report text.
integration_22_30: Connect classification, tagging, and pattern extraction into one coherent pipeline.
Test with genuinely tricky cases (a report that sounds severe but isn't actually SIF-potential by the research criteria, and vice versa) to confirm your classifier reflects the real distinction.
Build the interactive dashboard ranking sites/activities by SIF-precursor density.
polish_30_36: Polish the dashboard for genuine HSE-team usability.
Rehearse presenting your classification logic's grounding in the specific cited research frameworks.
Prepare to discuss a genuinely tricky classification example and why your model got it right.
build_plan.how_to_stand_out: Show your classifier correctly distinguishing a report that sounds dramatic but isn't genuinely SIF-potential from one that sounds mundane but reflects a genuine fatal-potential precursor pattern, grounded explicitly in the real research criteria your model is based on, that discrimination on the actual research distinction (not surface severity language) is the real point of this PS.

strengths: Very well-grounded in cited, real industry safety research, a credible foundation.
Direct, life-relevant impact case with clear intervention-prioritization value.
weaknesses: Real OIL safety report data isn't accessible, constructed sample data needs genuine realism.
Genuine SIF-precursor distinction (versus general severity) requires careful research grounding to get right.

roles_needed: Industrial safety/HSE domain-research person (critical, cited frameworks)
team_fit.ideal_ratio: Don't skip research into the specific cited SIF-precursor frameworks, that grounding is what makes this genuinely differentiated from a generic severity classifier.
team_fit.approach: Research the real IOGP Life-Saving Rules and cited SIF research before building your classification criteria.

ai_buildability_split.needs_human_judgment: Grounding classification criteria in the real, cited SIF-precursor research distinction (fatal-potential causes differ from general severity), that requires real safety-science domain research.
ai_buildability_split.risk_of_leaning_on_ai_only: A generic AI-scaffolded 'severity classifier' without genuine SIF-precursor research grounding would miss the actual, research-backed distinction this PS is specifically asking to operationalize, and could misdirect safety intervention resources.

data_resource_availability.status: No real OIL safety report data is accessible; realistic constructed sample reports grounded in real industry incident report patterns are the appropriate approach.
data_resource_availability.backup_plan: Construct sample reports based on publicly available industry safety incident report examples and the cited research frameworks' example precursor patterns.

judge_qna.question: How does your classification actually reflect the SIF-precursor distinction, not just general incident severity?

judge_qna.follow_up: What specific precursor patterns does your model consider most predictive of fatal potential?

judge_qna.question: How does your dashboard's site/activity ranking actually help HSE teams prioritize intervention?
judge_qna.strong_answer: Walk through a specific example showing how SIF-precursor density at a particular site/activity would translate into a concrete intervention recommendation.
judge_qna.follow_up: How would this integrate with OIL's existing HSSE platform and workflow?
